sections.skill: Tell cash basis from accrual basis with a timing example

questions.prompt: Under cash basis, when is income recorded?

choices.text: When the invoice is designed in software
When the customer first asks for a quote
When the work is advertised online

questions.intro: There are two common ways to record when income and expenses count. CASH BASIS records income when money is received and expenses when money is paid. ACCRUAL BASIS records income when it is earned (for example, when the work is done and invoiced) and expenses when they are incurred, even if payment happens later. Example: a job finished in December but paid in January counts as December income under accrual and January income under cash. Many small businesses start on cash basis; tax rules on which method may be used vary, so ask a tax professional.

sections.skill: Counting when you hand in homework versus when it is graded

questions.prompt: Counting when you finish the work is like which basis?
questions.intro: Imagine counting a homework assignment as "done" either when you finish it or when the teacher hands back the grade. Accrual is like counting it when you finish the work. Cash basis is like counting it when the grade (the money) comes back. The same assignment just lands on a different day depending on which rule you use.
